questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Release Management”?
options: Release Management helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Release Management means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Release Management removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Release Management should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Release Management helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Release Management is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Versioning application releases” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Versioning application releases” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Versioning application releases” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Versioning application releases” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Versioning application releases” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Versioning application releases” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Versioning application releases” under Release Management. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Release Management”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
